name: game-network
description: Step A0 of docs/design/game-reconstruction-and-motion.md: what Ocarina of Time's own anti-aliasing network costs on this GPU with each existing way of running its tensor instructions. Every variant runs the network (anti-aliasing Game, game presets off, frame generation off) with EDEN_NX2_TENSOR_LOG=1, which logs the path each tensor program takes: software (the default on Intel), the shared-memory software gather (EDEN_NX2_SW_MATRIX_SHARED) and 8x16x16 cooperative matrices (EDEN_NX2_INTEL_COOP_MATRIX), each against the software baseline, plus No sharpening, which replaces the network's output pass with a copy, as the floor. The 8x16x16 arm only changes anything on a GPU whose driver lists an 8x16x16 fp16 shape (Xe2: Arc 140V, B580); the Arc 140T lists 8x8x16 with fp32 accumulators only, so there it equals software and its log line says so. The network's cost is the output pass's GPU time in each row's gpu_costs (work, shader 6bd913e1f34e83eb). That shader is the pass with the Max Resolution add-on, which is on unless you disabled it (the log shows 'Applying built-in patch "Max Resolution (built-in)"'). A row counts only when its log has the EDEN_NX2_TENSOR_LOG line for 6bd913e1f34e83eb and no 'anti-aliasing network bypassed' line, except the no-sharpening row, which must have that line. Every arm translates the network afresh: run the suite twice in one session and read only the second pass, comparing its two software rows first.
